items.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo introduces a session-aware inference system designed to optimize agentic workloads that differ significantly from standard chat interactions. Unlike single-turn chats, agent sessions involve large initial prefills, repeated model calls, and parallel subagents, requiring a unified session-level identifier to manage context efficiently. The system transforms request-level infrastructure into a program-aware one, enabling session-aware routing, shared KV cache indexing, and programmatic cache movement across vLLM and SGLang. Key optimizations include session-aware admission control that applies backpressure at tool boundaries to reduce cache thrashing and a shared-pool indexer that accounts for reusable KV in external stores. Testing on SWE-bench showed a 12-16% throughput improvement over standard KV-routing alone at high concurrency, while maintaining a prefix-cache hit rate above 94.5%. The approach relies on a Session-Prefix Indexer and a proposed KvHint interface to coordinate policy intent from the router with execution in inference engines.
items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Introduces Session-Aware Agentic Inference System

items.summary: The White House blocked Microsoft and other firms from hiring skilled international workers permanently via the H1b visa program. Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of fraud and replacing American workers. Microsoft stated most filings were for existing employees paid equally to locals. The government halted new PERM applications for these companies.
items.title: White House Bars Microsoft From Permanent Foreign Worker Hiring

items.summary: Sixteen-year-old Bryce Vincent Gowryluk required emergency rescue after following incorrect directions from the AI chatbot Claude while attempting to climb in British Columbia. The incident highlights growing concerns regarding the reliability of artificial intelligence for wilderness navigation, prompting officials to warn hikers against blindly trusting digital maps that lack spatial awareness.
items.title: Teen Rescued After Relying on AI for Mountain Navigation

items.summary: OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, $20 billion less than the previously reported $70 billion figure. The Financial Times reported that the company shared this update with investors. OpenAI's IPO has been pushed to early 2027, and the company raised $122 billion in a March funding round.
items.title: OpenAI Revenue Reportedly Lower Than Projected

items.summary: Google announced the launch of a unified agentic AI for Gemini, designed to execute tasks autonomously. CEO Sundar Pichai noted Gemini has over 1 billion monthly active users and 90% of Fortune 100 businesses use Gemini Enterprise. Google will initially roll out the agent to businesses to address security and scale challenges before expanding to consumers. The agent can connect to internal systems and has its own Workspace account.
items.title: Google Announces Agentic AI for Business with Gemini

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Microsoft is changing its 365 Family, Premium, and Pro subscriptions to replace individual 1 TB OneDrive allowances with a shared pool. Family and Premium plans will see total shared storage drop from 6 TB to 2 TB, while the new Pro plan offers 5 TB for $100 monthly. Microsoft states these changes provide flexibility with AI and cloud storage benefits, rolling out shared storage starting Oct. 8, 2026. Subscribers exceeding the new limits may face price increases of $10 per additional TB. The article compares this to 'shrinkflation' and notes Microsoft's history of reducing storage limits.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Plans Face Storage Reductions and Potential Price Hikes

items.summary: The NVIDIA KGMON team placed second in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition by building a system focused on reliability through a constrained and inspectable harness. The approach involved normalizing data access, limiting the agent to a small set of tools, and implementing trace inspection to identify failures. Key techniques included schema scouting, persistent state management, and selective repeated attempts to handle uncertainty. The team emphasized that agent reliability depends less on model openness and more on the surrounding infrastructure, offering a playbook for building robust data analytics agents around smaller, fixed models.
items.title: NVIDIA KGMON Team Wins KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents Competition

items.summary: Airtel Money is listing on the London Stock Exchange, highlighting the growth of mobile money in Africa. While digital payments can help governments collect taxes by creating records of transactions, the article warns that without clear data protection rules, these systems risk alienating citizens. Drawing lessons from Australia's Robodebt scandal, the authors argue that governments must establish clear guardrails, involve taxpayers in system design, and ensure human oversight before automated enforcement. Without embedding trust and accountability, digital tax systems could damage the very ability of governments to levy revenue.
items.title: Data Protection Needed for African Tax Revenue from Digital Payments

items.summary: Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at Panmure Liberum, warns the AI trade could burst in 2027 or 2028, triggering the worst S&P 500 crash since 2008. He cites depleted hyperscaler cash flows and rising debt costs. While his 2027 target implies a 36% drop, he acknowledges his call may be premature and advises investors to prepare contingency plans rather than sell immediately.
items.title: Strategist Warns AI Bubble Risks Worst S&P 500 Crash Since 2008

items.summary: Deeptech firm PhysicsX opened an Asia-Pacific hub in Singapore to scale AI-powered industrial engineering. The company, backed by Temasek, aims to grow its local team and partner with entities to embed AI in manufacturing. A*STAR announced a partnership to develop engineering simulation capabilities, while PhysicsX highlighted its platform's ability to optimize complex designs.
items.title: PhysicsX Opens Singapore Hub to Scale AI Engineering

items.summary: Bay Area lettering artist Jesscia Hische designed the logo for Meta's new AI assistant, Muse, despite anticipating controversy. She explained that financial pressure from her small business in Oakland necessitated the freelance work. The project went viral on Threads, drawing criticism from designers who viewed working with Meta as a betrayal of ethical principles. Although Hische defended her decision and clarified she did not use AI in the design process, the backlash included personal attacks and speculation about her wealth. She expressed sadness over the misunderstanding but noted the incident highlighted fears regarding AI's impact on commercial art.
items.title: Designer Jesscia Hische Faces Backlash Over Meta AI Logo

items.summary: Bitdefender researchers discovered a malware campaign named 'Midnight Mimosa' embedded in the firmware of low-cost Android smartphones, primarily those using MediaTek chipsets. The malware allows attackers to silently install apps, perform ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies. It affects thousands of devices across more than 150 countries, with significant numbers in Mexico, France, Italy, the United States, Germany, Brazil, and Spain. The campaign was detected through Bitdefender's App Anomaly Detection technology, which flagged suspicious system applications. While some manufacturers released firmware updates to resolve infections, they have not publicly explained how the malware was introduced. Removing the infection requires firmware-level cleanup or disabling the malicious component using Android Debug Bridge, which can be complicated for many users.
items.title: Bitdefender Discovers Residential Proxy Malware on Low-Cost Android Phones

items.summary: Meta's AI agent, Muse, achieved the No. 1 spot on the U.S. App Store and gained millions of users in its first week. However, early adopters are deleting the app following reports that it accessed text messages and shared home addresses without permission. Meta states the tool runs in isolated virtual machines and asks before sending emails or making purchases.
items.title: Meta's AI Agent Gains Users Amid Privacy Fears

items.summary: Constellation Energy announced a partnership with Google to add 890 megawatts of generating capacity across 11 existing nuclear plants in the PJM Interconnection. The 20-year deal involves upgrading nonnuclear infrastructure to boost output without building new reactors, with a budget topping $4.3 billion. Constellation expects to complete the first uprate by 2028 and the entire batch in the early 2030s. While uprates offer a cost-effective way to add reliable capacity, analysts note that meeting the Trump administration's goal of 5 gigawatts of new nuclear capacity by 2029 will likely require new reactor construction as well.
items.title: Constellation and Google Partner for Nuclear Uprates to Boost Clean Power

items.summary: Rivian announced a 2026 Halloween update bringing Ghostbusters themes to its vehicles, featuring new UI cosmetics, light sequences, and an eerie voice assistant. The update, available on October 9 through November 2, includes games and applies to the R1 and R2 models. A physical ECTO-R1 concept was also created, starring Bill Murray in a promotional spot.
items.title: Rivian Unveils Ghostbusters-Themed Halloween Update for 2026

items.summary: BYD revealed the interior of its third-generation Tang electric SUV, featuring two large screens and zero-gravity captain's chairs. Lu Tian, general manager of BYD's Dynasty series, described the design as futuristic. The vehicle, set to launch later this year, includes Blade Batteries 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, promising rapid charging capabilities.
items.title: BYD Reveals Tech-Savvy Interior for Third-Generation Tang SUV

items.summary: President Trump declared on Truth Social that the U.S. will not attack Iran before the November Midterm Elections. This statement caused oil prices to drop, though they remain higher for the day. While the White House asked the Pentagon to prepare strike options, Trump's announcement suggests a desire to avoid escalating conflict before the vote. Iranian officials remain suspicious of the statement.
items.title: Trump Rules Out Iran Strikes Before Midterms, Oil Prices Plunge

items.summary: ContourGlobal has started construction on Project Sterling in Mohave County, Arizona, a 509-MW solar and 1.4-GWh storage facility. Tesla has signed a power purchase agreement for the site. Local teams will install over 760,000 solar modules and 300 battery containers, with a new 5.2-mile road being built to access the location. The project aims to provide clean power for up to 16 hours daily.
items.title: ContourGlobal Begins Construction on Arizona Solar and Storage Project

items.summary: Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall as a Category 2 storm between Mississippi and the Florida Panhandle. This marks the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, breaking the satellite-era record for the latest first storm by nearly a month. Experts attribute the delay to El Niño, which created unfavorable wind and humidity conditions, though the storm still poses a threat with potential 7-foot storm surges.
items.title: Hurricane Isaias Breaks Atlantic Season Record With Late Arrival

items.summary: More than 120 US lawmakers raised concerns on Thursday regarding Alphabet's Google unit acquiring Spirit Airlines' internal data for $10 million to train artificial intelligence systems. Led by Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Steven Horsford, the lawmakers noted the sale includes 100 million emails and 500 million Microsoft Teams messages. They requested the company exclude employee information from the transaction to the greatest extent possible.
items.title: Lawmakers Oppose Google Acquisition of Spirit Airlines Data for AI Training

items.summary: Apple appointed Steve Smith as head of mergers and acquisitions while moving Adrian Perica to lead its services division, according to a memo seen by Reuters. Perica, a 17-year veteran, now oversees iCloud and other businesses. Eddy Cue stated in the memo that the move allows for more focus on services. Apple shares rose about 1.4 per cent on Thursday.
items.title: Apple Appoints Steve Smith as M&A Chief and Shifts Adrian Perica to Services

items.summary: The White House announced that President Donald Trump will present the nation's highest honours for scientific and technological achievement. Recipients include technology industry leaders Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Michael Dell, who are set to receive the National Medal of Science and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
items.title: Trump to honour Musk and Huang with top US science medals

items.summary: Anthropic published an updated usage policy effective November 12 that prohibits sustained abusive behavior toward its Claude models and clarifies restrictions on election interference, weapons development, and surveillance. The policy targets extreme scenarios of cruelty while allowing critical feedback and research. It also addresses the use of the AI for spreading false information and running fake accounts, drawing on observed misuse patterns from a threat intelligence report.
items.title: Anthropic Updates AI Usage Policy to Ban Abuse and Misuse

items.summary: Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Haiku 5.5, a compact AI model. The company stated that token prices for this version are reduced by as much as 90% compared to the prior iteration. This pricing strategy targets routine, large-scale enterprise workloads.
items.title: Anthropic Cuts AI Model Prices by Up to 90%

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services hired 4,258 employees on a net basis in the September 2026 quarter, according to a fact sheet released on October 8. This marks the third consecutive quarter of net headcount growth for the company. The final headcount stood at 598,056. During the first half of the fiscal year, TCS added around 9,279 employees, bringing total net headcount additions to 13,537.
items.title: TCS Reports Third Consecutive Quarter of Net Headcount Growth

items.summary: Coca-Cola is re-evaluating the sale of Costa Coffee, a British coffeehouse chain it acquired for $5.1 billion in 2018. The company has faced challenges growing the business, which lost nearly £20 million in 2023 and 2024. A previous sales attempt in late 2025 failed due to tepid interest from private-equity bidders. Costa Coffee, with 2,700 outlets in the UK and Ireland, continues to expand its menu and plans to open a new headquarters in Hertfordshire in January 2027.
items.title: Coca-Cola Re-Explores Selling Costa Coffee Amidst Struggles

items.summary: Protesters in Madrid attribute Spain's housing crisis to vulture funds and investment firms that buy properties to hike rents. While the Spanish government and activists cite these actors, experts like Jorge Galindo argue that data shows company ownership of rentals is low. He attributes rising costs primarily to a severe shortage of supply compared to demand, exacerbated by demographic changes and lagging salaries. A study by Idealista notes rental costs rose 84% over ten years, with higher increases in Málaga and Marbella. Despite a housing shortfall of around 750,000 homes, the government's proposed reforms were rejected, prompting a snap election.
items.title: Protesters Blame Vulture Funds for Spain's Housing Crisis

items.summary: Leaked audio of Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton criticizing federal programs and the Republican convention has prompted handwringing among GOP officials. While Republicans deny the remarks are fatal, they fear the leaks fuel perceptions of disarray in a tight race against Democrat James Talarico. Former Senate Leadership Fund leader Steven Law noted Paxton lacks experience at this level, and Senator John Cornyn advised him to be more careful. National Republican Senatorial Campaign spokesperson Joanna Rodriguez urged unity, warning against disarray in the home state of the modern Republican Party.
items.title: Leaked Audio of Ken Paxton Sparks Republican Concern Over Campaign Strategy

items.summary: Goldman Sachs top executives are set to share a bonus pot of up to $500m, marking one of the bank's largest payouts in history. The $100m reward for CEO David Solomon is made of stock and exceeds his previous year's pay. The bonuses, tied to stock performance over five years, aim to retain talent in a competitive market.
items.title: Goldman Sachs Top Executives Set for Massive Bonus Payout

items.summary: The author predicts that AI will delegate mathematical tasks, improving top-tier research while human-led studies focus on qualitative interviews and field experiments. Administrative data analysis may benefit prolific authors, while economic history could see a boom from digitizing archives. Conversely, routine research might be outsourced to public agencies, potentially harming researchers dependent on such work. Review systems will likely improve with AI assistance.
items.title: Predictions for Economics and Social Sciences with AI Integration

items.summary: The Ministry of Defence objected to at least four planned windfarms in the past year, citing fears that spinning blades could cause unacceptable interference with military radar. Specific concerns were raised regarding the Hope Moor project in County Durham and an offshore array in the Irish Sea. While industry sources note such issues usually lead to minor adjustments rather than cancellations, the MoD's interventions continue to create tension with energy security goals.
items.title: MoD Objects to Windfarms Over Radar Interference Fears

items.summary: Alibaba has filed a lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Defense, challenging its classification as a Chinese military affiliate under Section 1260H. The Pentagon lists Alibaba alongside Baidu and Tencent as entities subject to procurement bans due to alleged ties to China's state-directed military-civil fusion strategy. Alibaba denies these accusations, arguing the listing lacks factual or legal basis and violates its constitutional rights. The DoD cites evidence including Alibaba's compliance with Chinese censorship laws, its involvement in state-backed joint ventures, and its strategic investments in sectors like space and energy as proof of alignment with Chinese government interests.
items.title: Alibaba Sues Pentagon Over Military Affiliate Classification

items.summary: A High Court judge ruled that search warrants used by Thames Valley Police against former Prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor were unlawful. While the police acknowledged the error, the investigation continues. The court must still decide if seized items can be retained. Mountbatten-Windsor remains under investigation following his arrest in February regarding links to Jeffrey Epstein, which he has denied.
items.title: Ex-Prince Andrew Wins Challenge Over Unlawful Police Warrants

items.summary: Petitioners are requesting a two-year trial of a designated pet-friendly carriage on all NSW trains and metro services. Over 6,500 people have signed the petition, which requires dogs to be on a lead or in a carrier. Transport for NSW welcomes the feedback, noting similar past campaigns have been unsuccessful. The petition aims to address current restrictions that disadvantage non-car owners.
items.title: Petitioners seek trial for pet-friendly carriages on NSW trains and metro services

items.summary: On October 8, 2026, Canadian and Icelandic foreign ministers met in Reykjavik to urge a stronger NATO presence in the Arctic and North Atlantic. According to a statement by Global Affairs Canada, the ministers emphasized shared commitments to security and stability in the region. They also discussed trade opportunities, defense cooperation, and the modernization of the Free Trade Agreement involving Iceland and other EFTA members.
items.title: Canada and Iceland Call for Enhanced NATO Presence in Arctic and North Atlantic

items.summary: Tony Maple, a heritage researcher, argues a new waterfront stadium proposal conflicts with the original design by Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin. While Canberra Airport unveiled plans for a 25,000-35,000 seat venue, Maple warns it could encroach on Commonwealth Park and Lake Burley Griffin. ACT Planning Minister Chris Steel noted the render looked incredible but requires further study regarding transport and parking impacts.
items.title: Historian questions if proposed Canberra stadium matches Griffins' original vision

items.summary: At the World Judo Championships in Baku, Ai Tsunoda Roustant claimed her first senior world title at -70kg by defeating Michaela Polleres in golden score. In the -90kg final, Sanshiro Murao retained his title with a spectacular ippon against Goki Tajima, becoming a two-time world champion. International Judo Federation officials awarded the medals.
items.title: Ai Tsunoda and Sanshiro Murao Win World Judo Titles in Baku

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked a donor to wire $100,000 to her American Express account before her Senate confirmation. Messages show she sought funds and offered access to officials. Eric Deters, the donor, refused the request and stated he paid Guilfoyle $300,000 in speaking fees since 2020. Guilfoyle's lawyer disputes the messages' authenticity.
items.title: US Envoy to Greece Asked Donor for Wire Transfer

items.summary: Prosecutors in the Department of Justice's civil rights division are seeking criminal charges against Cassidy Hutchinson for alleged lies to Congress regarding her testimony on the January 6 attack. Hutchinson, a former White House aide, described interactions with Mark Meadows and Donald Trump. While Republicans dispute her account, the Justice Department has not confirmed the investigation. Previous similar indictments were dismissed due to unlawful appointments.
items.title: Prosecutors Seek Charges Against Ex-Trump Aide Over Capitol Testimony

items.summary: Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, is forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, hurricane-force winds, and heavy rainfall to the US Gulf Coast. Currently a category 1 hurricane with sustained winds of 85mph, it is expected to strengthen as it approaches the northern Gulf Coast on Friday. Millions of people from Louisiana to Florida are under warnings, with state of emergency declarations issued in Georgia, Alabama, and Florida. Officials urge residents to prepare for impacts including flooding, power outages, and potential tornadoes as the storm moves toward landfall late Friday or early Saturday.
items.title: Hurricane Isaias Brings Dangerous Storm Surge and Widespread Warnings to US Gulf Coast

items.summary: Julien's Auctions is selling over 100 items from Michael Jackson's career, including his iconic glove and red leather jacket, in Abu Dhabi. Martin Nolan estimates the glove could fetch $600,000 to $800,000, while the jacket is expected to sell for more than $10 million. The auction coincides with renewed interest in Jackson following the release of a biopic.
items.title: Michael Jackson memorabilia auctioned in Abu Dhabi

items.summary: The World Food Programme is seeking over $30 million to sustain food assistance for Congolese refugees in Burundi. Without additional funding, supplies could deplete by October 2026. While recent donor contributions prevented an immediate interruption, the agency estimates assistance will last only a few more months. The camp currently hosts around 33,000 refugees.
items.title: WFP Urges Funding to Feed Congolese Refugees in Burundi

items.summary: In April 2026, the Brazilian government prohibited the import of meat from endangered angelsharks. Despite this ban, angelsharks remain freely sold in the South of Brazil, where local governments have placed new orders for the product. Three public agencies stated they would suspend purchase plans after being contacted by Mongabay. Experts note that compliance is hampered by the sale of shark meat under the generic name “cação.” Data from the Federal Revenue Service shows significant imports of angelshark species between 2021 and September 2026. IBAMA published a regulation banning all shark imports on March 27, 2026, which took effect on April 3. However, vendors in Porto Alegre remain unaware of the rule or skeptical of its enforcement. Environmental agencies cite inadequate infrastructure and a shortage of enforcement agents as barriers to stopping the trade. Sea Shepherd Brasil filed a lawsuit against the Ministry of Health regarding recommendations to serve shark meat to children.
items.title: Brazil bans angelshark imports but illegal trade continues in markets

items.summary: Adidas has sued Australian retailer White Fox, alleging its four-striped clothing design is deceptively similar to Adidas's trademarked three-stripe logo. The German brand claims White Fox infringed its reputation and is seeking damages. White Fox, founded in 2013, reported revenue of AU$542m in the 12 months to June 2025. The first court hearing is scheduled for Friday, with both sides declining comment.
items.title: Adidas Sues White Fox Over Deceptively Similar Four-Stripe Design

items.summary: Activists in Arizona and Sonora are opposing a U.S. border wall construction, arguing it fragments habitats and blocks wildlife corridors. The movement centers on protecting ancient cottonwood trees, including one dubbed the 'Grandmother Tree,' which activists occupied for over 70 days. The protest links ecological preservation with social justice, involving groups like No More Deaths and the Tohono O’odham Nation. Authorities have used surveillance and force, including removing tree sitters, while activists continue to resist, citing the need to protect biodiversity and community connections across borders.
items.title: Activists Block Border Wall to Protect Trees and Wildlife

items.summary: The Kurdish PKK group accused the Turkish state of failing to pursue the peace process effectively, despite withdrawing all combat forces from Turkiye. The group stated this withdrawal was to prevent the government from making excuses. A 2024 law offers limited amnesty, but the fate of jailed leader Abdullah Ocalan remains unspecified. The PKK demands his freedom as a key step in ending the decades-long conflict that has killed roughly 50,000 people.
items.title: PKK Accuses Turkish State of Inadequate Peace Process Efforts

items.summary: Tens of thousands of students and supporters gathered in Paris and across France on October 8, 2026, to protest against poor education conditions and police brutality. Demonstrators blocked hundreds of high schools, citing absent teachers, overcrowded schedules, and unsafe facilities. While Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu promised a response plan by the end of October, students expressed skepticism, demanding concrete action rather than words. The unrest has resulted in injuries and over 6,500 arrests, prompting police to suspend the use of stun grenades after an incident involving a 15-year-old student. Government officials, including Education Minister Edouard Geffray, have pledged emergency measures to address teacher shortages and resource allocation within the 2027 budget.
items.title: French Students Protest Education Crisis and Police Force

items.summary: Lotus confirmed Charli XCX, Travis Scott, and The Killers as headliners for the 15th Lollapalooza Chile Festival, scheduled for March 12 through 14, 2027, at Parque O'Higgins in Santiago. Ticket prices range from 242,000 pesos for a general pass to 1,306,000 pesos for a Platinum pass with exclusive services.
items.title: Charli XCX, Travis Scott and The Killers headline Lollapalooza Chile 2027

items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels captured Yemen's Perim Island in September, bringing a major Middle East conflict close to Africa's Red Sea coast. The island controls the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical shipping lane. Since the Gaza war began in 2023, Houthis have targeted merchant ships, causing economic strain and a refugee crisis. At least 3,700 refugees crossed into Djibouti since September 10, with the UNHCR preparing to assist another 10,000. Ethiopia, which relies on Djibouti for 95% of its trade, faces rising costs and internal instability. Regional tensions remain high as diplomatic ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea are severed.
items.title: Houthi Conflict Disrupts Red Sea Trade and Displaces Refugees in Horn of Africa

items.summary: French, US, and Russian astronauts returned to Earth on Thursday after an eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station. SpaceX facilitated their splashdown in the Pacific off Los Angeles. The crew replaced four station occupants who departed early due to a medical evacuation. Jessica Meir noted the crew's excitement and mixed emotions upon returning home.
items.title: French, US and Russian Astronauts Return to Earth After Eight-Month Mission

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee raised interest rates by 25 bps to combat rising inflation, projecting retail inflation at 4.9% in Q2. Driven by global oil prices exceeding $100 a barrel and a deficient monsoon, the central bank shifted its stance to 'calibrated tightening' to manage inflation expectations while forecasting 7.1% GDP growth for 2026-27.
items.title: RBI Hikes Rates Amid Rising Inflation and Oil Prices

items.summary: A filing from the US Office of Government Ethics details 517 transactions by President Trump, including stakes worth at least $1 million in various companies and Meta stock valued between $5 million and $25 million. The Trump Organisation states that independent institutions manage these holdings and that transactions occur through automated processes without Trump's involvement.
items.title: Trump Discloses Major Tech and Energy Stock Purchases

items.summary: Infosys and Wipro ADRs declined following TCS's strong quarterly earnings and US administration actions suspending several tech firms from the PERM green card programme. Vice President JD Vance and Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling cited abuse of the programme and federal investigations as reasons for the suspensions, which include Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini. The moves raise concerns for Indian IT companies relying on the US market.
items.title: Infosys and Wipro stocks fell after TCS earnings and US immigration crackdown

items.summary: The US government suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program following an investigation led by Vice President JD Vance. Officials accused the company of abusing the system by replacing American workers with foreign hires. Microsoft pushed back, stating most H-1B filings were for existing employees. The suspension remains indefinite until the probe concludes.
items.title: US Suspends Microsoft from Green Card Program Over Alleged Abuse

items.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi supported Elon Musk's claims regarding Starlink's delayed launch in India. The Ministry of Communications refuted allegations of unfair treatment, stating all satellite firms are at a similar regulatory stage. Musk alleged oligarchs block the company, while Starlink's VP noted investments in 20 gateway sites and local data controls. Security assessments are currently underway for all licensees.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Elon Musk against Starlink delays in India

items.summary: On the same day Vice President JD Vance criticized Microsoft for using foreign workers, President Donald Trump prepared to honor CEO Satya Nadella with top technology awards. Vance stated the administration supports Microsoft but will deny permanent residency applications until the company prioritizes hiring American workers. The announcement highlights a contrast between honoring leadership and enforcing domestic hiring policies.
items.title: Trump Honors Nadella While Vance Criticizes Microsoft Hiring Practices

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India issued notices to Dr Reddy's, Nestle Health Science, and e-commerce platforms for selling the 'CELEVIDA GLP' supplement with misleading health claims. The regulator stated that advertisements implying the product supports muscle preservation during GLP-1 therapies were non-compliant. Amazon confirmed the product is no longer available on its marketplace, while other companies have not yet responded to the allegations.
items.title: FSSAI Issues Notices to Companies Over Misleading Protein Supplement Claims

items.summary: Elon Musk questioned why Starlink lacks an Indian licence despite complying with local laws for five years and operating in 165 other countries. He alleged that oligarchs were blocking the service. In response, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi cryptically replied, "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." The Indian government rejected Musk's claims as baseless, stating its regulatory framework is fair and non-discriminatory. While Starlink holds a GMPCS licence, it awaits security clearance and spectrum assignment before commercial operations can begin. The ministry noted that Starlink, along with Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications, is currently undergoing security assessments.
items.title: Musk Questions Starlink India Licence Delay Amid Regulatory Scrutiny

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 0.25 per cent, a move expected to lower net asset values and yields for fixed-income mutual funds in the short term. Experts note that while existing bond values may decline, investors can benefit from reinvesting at higher rates as markets stabilize. The central bank has also shifted its policy stance to 'calibrated tightening,' signaling an extended period of rate hikes.
items.title: RBI Rate Hike Expected to Reduce Debt Fund NAVs and Yields

items.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier requested a court order forcing Meta to remove users under 14 from Facebook and Instagram and limit teen usage to two hours daily. Uthmeier argued the company engineered addictive platforms, rejecting a prior settlement involving 48 states and $18 billion. Meta denied wrongdoing and urged Florida to target other platforms like YouTube and TikTok instead.
items.title: Florida Sues Meta to Restrict Teen Access to Facebook and Instagram

items.summary: The Madras High Court Registry lodged a police complaint alleging that five Bangladesh nationals forged court proceedings to secure their deportation. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan ordered the verification after petitioners submitted fake clearance documents. The Registrar confirmed the documents were forged, and the Registry filed the complaint with the Greater Chennai Commissioner of Police on October 6, 2026, requesting a status report by November 10, 2026.
items.title: Madras High Court Registry files police complaint over forged deportation orders

items.summary: The Indian government reported that 16 seafarers were killed in attacks, with 11 in the Persian Gulf and five in the Black Sea over nearly eight months. A senior Saudi official at the Sagarmanthan Dialogue condemned the seizure of sealanes as a criminal act, stating that international waterways must not be controlled by any single entity. Officials noted that 74 vessels of Indian interest, including 25 India-flagged ships, have transited the Strait of Hormuz.
items.title: Saudi Official Condemns Seizure of Sealanes After Indian Seafarers Killed

items.summary: The death of veteran actor Nana Patekar at 75 has highlighted the critical nature of sudden cardiac arrest. Doctors state that bystanders should initiate hands-only CPR immediately rather than waiting for training. Dr Rakesh Garg notes survival chances decrease by 7% to 10% with every minute without intervention, emphasizing the need for prompt action during such medical emergencies.
items.title: Nana Patekar's Death Highlights Urgency of Immediate CPR Intervention

items.summary: Forest officials in East Godavari district reported that a tiger has moved from the Rampachodavaram forest into plain areas near Devarapalli. Officials advised residents not to venture out alone and stated that capture efforts are underway. A team of forest experts from Pune is expected to arrive on Friday to assist. Gopalapuram MLA Maddipati Venkata Raju directed officials to regularly caution people about the tiger's movement.
items.title: Tiger Moves Into Plain Areas In East Godavari District

items.summary: Delhi Police's Crime Branch registered a fresh FIR to investigate the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march, examining the role of 2,873 individuals with criminal records. Sources stated the probe aims to determine if the violence was premeditated. The Supreme Court allowed this specific FIR after quashing earlier cases, while investigators verify identities and reconstruct events regarding injuries and property damage.
items.title: Delhi Police Register Fresh FIR Against 2,873 Individuals Over July 20 Violence

items.summary: Citizens in New Delhi remain divided over whether to join an October 10 protest demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Police have issued prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and are actively mobilizing residents and students to refrain from participating, warning that unsanctioned gatherings disrupt law and order. While some locals fear detention and refuse to support the protest, youth organizations and residents' welfare groups continue door-to-door campaigns, asserting the right to protest and highlighting the impact of SIR on marginalized workers. Authorities have restricted transport and communication services on the day of the protest.
items.title: Citizens Divided on October 10 Protest Calls Amid Police Warnings

items.summary: Police in Indore arrested two men, Abhishek and Raj, for throwing a liquor-like substance at a woman in Saket Nagar on Oct 3. The suspects allegedly planned the attack after the victim rejected Raj's marriage proposals and cut off communication. Police identified them using CCTV footage and the victim's statement, and further investigation is underway.
items.title: Two Men Arrested in Indore for Attacking Woman with Liquor-Like Substance

items.summary: Pakistan cricketer Umar Akmal paid tribute to veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar, who died at 75 in Goa after a cardiac arrest. Patekar, known for films like Krantiveer and a three-time National Film Award winner, received full state honours in Pune. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also described his contribution to cinema as immense.
items.title: Cricketer Umar Akmal Mourns Veteran Actor Nana Patekar's Death

items.summary: Political parties in Telangana and Bengaluru staged protests against the Special Intensive Revision process, alleging voter deletion and lack of transparency. Leaders demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav visited Ayodhya for a Sanatan outreach event, highlighting a contest over Hindutva messaging ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections. Former judges and opposition leaders also addressed concerns regarding the Election Commission's credibility.
items.title: Political Parties Protest Voter Deletions and Akhilesh Yadav Visits Ayodhya

items.summary: Opposition parties staged protests in Bengaluru and Hyderabad demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They allege the Special Intensive Revision process disenfranchises voters and lacks transparency. While Congress leaders claim thousands of voters were removed, the Election Commission defends the exercise under the Representation of the People Act, warning that unsubstantiated claims could erode public faith in elections.
items.title: Opposition Parties Demand CEC Resignation Over Voter List Disputes

items.summary: The GST Council approved a concept note for an optional compliance scheme allowing small businesses with turnover up to ₹5 crore to file one annual return while making quarterly payments. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated the detailed framework will be considered at the next meeting.
items.title: GST Council Approves Optional Quarterly Tax Scheme for Small Businesses

items.summary: Ravi Sam, the newly elected chairman of the Cotton Textile Export Promotion Council, stated that the organization will prioritize increasing branded 'Kasturi Cotton Bharat' production over the next two years. He noted that currently, less than 50% of cotton meets mandatory specifications. Sam also highlighted the benefits of Free Trade Agreements for Indian garment exporters and mentioned that the Confederation of Indian Industry- Southern Region is conducting sessions to assist them.
items.title: Texprocil Chairman Ravi Sam Outlines Focus on Kasturi Cotton and FTA Benefits

items.summary: Rajendra Sapate, a 55-year-old farmer in Maharashtra's Bhandara district, died by jumping into a well following crop failure due to drought. Officials state he had previously petitioned for irrigation without success. Minister Pankaj Bhoyar visited the area to review conditions, acknowledging the severity. Police registered an accidental death case while relatives declined to press charges. State leaders have sought central assistance as 80% of talukas face severe drought.
items.title: Maharashtra Farmer Dies After Drought Petitions Ignored

items.summary: The Union government capped trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30% of the maximum retail price to reduce patient expenditure. Based on data showing mark-ups up to 700%, the measure aims to lower costs in a market with an annual turnover of approximately ₹12,500 crore. Officials expect price reductions of up to 70% and annual savings of around ₹2,500 crore, drawing on a 2019 intervention model.
items.title: India caps trade margins on non-scheduled cancer drugs at 30% of MRP
